content.text: {"edits":[{"path":"First_Phase/scene_demo/finish_v1/vision.py","old":"        \"Before released/clear_of_target=true, inspect fingertip-to-target AND fingertip-to-support gaps in each useful view. Visible touch or wrap around a bottle neck/rim means false; if the fingertip gap is occluded or tips cannot be identified and no other view resolves it, use null, not an assertion that fingers are retracted. Do not infer lack of contact solely from the main object's body being clear.\",","new":"        \"Before released/clear_of_target=true, inspect fingertip-to-target AND fingertip-to-support gaps in each useful view. When the complete hand silhouette, including fingers, is clearly and consistently distant from both target and support across mutually corroborating views, and the target is independently supported by the destination, macroscopic separation permits released/clear_of_target true even if fine pad edges are not individually resolvable; do not require a tiny contact gap or a historical release motion. Only when views are close, projectively overlapping, or wrapping a bottle neck/rim must the actual fingertip-to-target and fingertip-to-support gaps be observed: visible touch means false, and an occluded gap with no other view disambiguating it means null. Keep full fingertip identification, and do not use an erroneous bbox that circles only the wrist housing to prove retraction; open encoder alone still cannot prove release. For place, operation_achieved means placement plus support only, independently of released and clear_of_target. Use direct image evidence, not fixed pixel coordinates, scene positions, or any sample answer key; do not force bbox rules to true and do not alter any boolean criterion.\","}]}
